From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 09 Oct 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 QBR prep: pipeline underwrite, account-level one-pagers, OKR gating

Team —

We need a tight, leadership-ready packet for the QBR readout next week. Goal: one consolidated forecast that leadership can sign off on, plus account-by-account one-pagers for any deals > $250K or at high risk. Please do the following by EOD Tuesday (10/12):

- Update forecast in HubSpot (commit/oppty stage + reason) for every open opportunity.
- Fill out the attached qbr_account_template.xlsx for your top 6 signal accounts (3 prioritized for the QBR + 3 spares). Include: close plan, blockers, procurement contacts, and ask.
- Flag any deals where procurement/legal are holding (include contact details).

I attached the template (qbr_account_template.xlsx) and an example one-pager. If you have a competing estimate for ACME, include it in HubSpot and add a short note in the template.

Primary ask: Jordan, Marcus — can you own consolidation (Jordan does accounts A–M; Marcus does N–Z). Tessa, please synthesize the rollup and surface OKR gating items (risk to ARR goal). Aditya — nudges on renewals and finance-related line-items.

We will circulate the consolidated packet by 11/13 09:00 PT so execs have time to review before the QBR.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Note: one large expansion (Big Retail Corp) is in legal hold — procurement@big-retail.com requested more SOC2 artifacts; I'm looping Aditya for the compliance evidence.

I'll hand the accounts A–M consolidated sheet to Marcus by EOD tomorrow so he can drop into the rollup.

-Jordan

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. I consolidated the submissions into a single leadership packet (consolidated-qbr-packet-20271013.pdf) and pulled the HubSpot rollup (HS-234789) and DocuSign status for top deals. High-level:

- Commit vs target: Commit = 58%; Best-case = 82%. Gap: $1.9M (mainly four accounts flagged with procurement/legal holds).
- OKR gating: Renewal velocity and procurement friction are the top risks that could impact Q4 ARR OKR if unresolved by mid-November.
- Top escalations (accounts requiring leadership intervention):
  1) Acme Enterprises — procurement hold, needs on-prem pricing appendix and legal exception for data residency. Customer contact: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-enterprises.com>.
  2) Big Retail Corp — SOC2 artifacts requested; finance wants accelerated evidence.
  3) CloudSvc (expansion) — pricing negotiation; Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudsvc.io> asked for a commercial concession memo.

Next steps: Vivek, I propose a 30-minute prep slot tomorrow (10/14) to walk execs through the packet and the required leadership asks. I also flagged three OKR actions in the packet that require cross-functional commitments: (1) SOC2 evidence prioritization, (2) short-term on-prem appendix, (3) prioritized CS/SE support for procurement calls.

If no objections, I'll route the packet to execs at 09:00 PT on 10/14.

-Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
